trust_decision.summary: Decided: untrusted text files enter at OBConversion::ReadFile / the obabel CLI and are parsed by per-format handler plugins; the protection is that a reader must never index its fixed local vector3 translationVectors[3] past 2, and each handler has to enforce that bound itself where it counts rows, because no shared validation layer exists.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names MOPAC 'UNIT CELL TRANSLATION', and this is the block that reads those rows and does translationVectors[numTranslationVectors++].Set(x, y, z) with no bound on numTranslationVectors.

fix_sites.module_kind: format reader plugin (MOPAC output), reached through the public OBConversion API

fix_sites.entry_point: OBConversion::ReadFile / obabel -imopout -> MOPACFormat::ReadMolecule, 'FINAL  POINT  AND  DERIVATIVES' block

fix_sites.module_kind: format reader plugin (Gaussian output), a different module family
format reader plugin (MSI/Cerius2), a different module family

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/formats/msiformat.cpp:149-157 (MSI reader) and src/formats/gaussformat.cpp:597-625 (Gaussian output reader) - independent parsers that rebuild the same translation-vector information from a different file syntax

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is CVE-2022-46292, whose title is the MOPAC output 'UNIT CELL TRANSLATION' block; the MSI and Gaussian readers are different formats, with their own CVE IDs (CVE-2022-46295, CVE-2022-46291) and their own parsers, so a solver can argue they belong to other advisories and leave them unguarded.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The block must keep consuming rows after the 3rd translation vector: the Gaussian loop treats atom rows and Tv rows inside one while loop, so a break or return false on the 4th row stops reading whatever rows follow; and every reader still has to build an OBUnitCell from as few as one or two vectors because the attach sites gate on numTranslationVectors > 0, so requiring exactly 3 before SetData breaks legitimate partial cells.

O6_input_shapes: MOPAC output 'UNIT CELL TRANSLATION' block: 5-token rows 'n Tv x y z' (src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:164-170)
MOPAC output 'FINAL  POINT  AND  DERIVATIVES' block: 8-token rows where only the 'Tv CART Z' row of each vector writes the array (src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:184-216)
MOPAC Cartesian input .mop: atom rows whose element symbol is 'Tv', 6- or 7-token lines (src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:720-729)
Gaussian output orientation block: rows whose atomic number is -2 ('Tv') among ordinary atom rows (src/formats/gaussformat.cpp:606-625)
MSI (Cerius2): 'PeriodicType' record followed by 6-token '(A D X3 (x y z))' rows (src/formats/msiformat.cpp:149-157)

O7_producer.where: src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:96,159,164-170 - each reader keeps its own local numTranslationVectors counter and bumps it in the same tokenising loop that writes the array; there is no schema, serializer or shared producer layer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an rprim reader that takes a leading count line and loops the unguarded translationVectors[numTranslationVectors++] over that many rows
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This branch already writes the same 3-element array unguarded and is safe only because of the hard-coded for (int i = 1; i < 4; ++i); the neighbouring acell and typat branches read a count or a token list first, so extending rprim the same way is the obvious next maintainer edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second PeriodicType/lattice record type that appends more vectors to the same array
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The block already appends every 6-token row after PeriodicType without resetting the counter, so adding support for another record type copies an append loop that has no bound.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second periodic-vector branch (another PRIMVEC/CONVVEC shape, e.g. an ANIMSTEPS variant) that copies this loop but drops the numTranslationVectors < 3 condition
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Here the bound lives only inside the while condition, so a maintainer adding a sibling branch for a new keyword naturally copies the body and keeps just the tokenising and the unguarded increment.

O9_family: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787 / CWE-119) into a fixed 3-element stack array indexed by an unvalidated row counter

O10_build.toolchain: CMake >= 3.10 plus a C++ compiler; optional Eigen3, Boost (filesystem, iostreams, unit_test_framework), libxml2, zlib, Cairo; inchi is bundled unless OPENBABEL_USE_SYSTEM_INCHI is set (CMakeLists.txt:137-149); format readers build as shared plugin modules
O10_build.project_tests: test/fuzzregresstest.cpp provides RunRepro() (OBConversion::ReadFile on a corpus file) wired through test/CMakeLists.txt fuzzregress_parts, which at the pinned commit covers cases 1-4 only (test/CMakeLists.txt:35); the fix adds cases 5-9 plus test/files/fuzz_regress/cve-2022-4629*. test/testgauss.py round-trips g09. No existing read tests assert a unit cell for mopout/mop/g09/msi translation vectors.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add if (numTranslationVectors < 3) at the MOPAC 'UNIT CELL TRANSLATION' write only (src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:170), reproduce with a .out containing four Tv rows, and declare the format fixed.

out_of_scope_notes: Same array, different weakness: the attach sites still call uc->SetData(translationVectors[0], [1], [2]) when only 1-2 vectors were read, so the missing elements are uninitialized reads (src/formats/msiformat.cpp:270-272, src/formats/gaussformat.cpp:1360-1362, src/formats/mopacformat.cpp:741-746); that is not this advisory's out-of-bounds write and the fix does not change it.
